source.title: By carrot or by stick: cognitive reinforcement learning in parkinsonism.

confidence_rationale: Canonical human dissociation predicted by a model with separate Go/NoGo pathways: dopamine state flips the positive-vs-negative learning bias. Strong source; mapping to ARC-109 is partial because the dissociation is in LEARNING, which the claim explicitly notes already existed in REE, and the split's selection-layer role is inferred rather than tested.
failure_signatures: The dissociation is between learning from positive versus negative outcomes; it does not by itself show that Go and No-Go must stay separate at CHOICE time rather than being summed after learning.
Parkinson's patients off/on medication differ in more than striatal dopamine (frontal dopamine, disease duration), so the Go/NoGo attribution rests on the model.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Parkinson's patients off dopaminergic medication learn better to avoid choices with negative outcomes than to pick choices with positive outcomes; medication reverses the bias. This pattern was predicted by a basal ganglia model with separate Go and NoGo pathways differentially modulated by positive and negative reinforcement.
mapping.ree_translation: Human evidence that low versus high dopamine produces OPPOSITE asymmetries across two dissociable pathways -- the D1-LTP / D2-LTD asymmetry that ARC-108's signed RPE implements and that ARC-109's two populations are the substrate for. It also anchors the claim's psychiatric axis: a Parkinson-analog (dopamine-depleted) organism should show a NoGo-dominated profile a single-scalar lesion does not produce.
mapping.mapping_caveat: The paper measures learning asymmetry, which ARC-109's own boundary statement says is NOT its subject (the learning-update asymmetry 'already existed'); the selection-layer split is the model's architecture, not what the behaviour isolates. Clinical dopamine depletion is also far coarser than REE's d2_da_gain lesion knob.
mapping.source_context: Human patients with Parkinson's disease on/off medication versus controls; probabilistic selection and transitive-inference procedural learning tasks; neural network model of basal ganglia-dopamine interactions.

confidence_components.notes: Top venue, widely replicated paradigm; mapping downgraded because the measured asymmetry is in learning, not in the selection-layer representation ARC-109 is about.
